[A1] The Axiom of Choice is assumed; it implies the countable-choice assumptions in the differential-geometric suppliers. No stronger choice principle is introduced. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F2] Under countable choice a nonempty connected complete boundaryless Riemannian manifold has a minimizing geodesic between any two points. Here every indicated component is compact and hence complete. ([[thm-hopf-rinow]], [[thm-compact-implies-complete-and-totally-bounded]]).

[F1] The family relations, normalized trace metric, algebraic loci $\widehat P_j$, and compatibility convention define the spaces used here. ([[def-orthogonal-clifford-families-and-centrioles]]).



**Proof technique:** direct construction.

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 Trace cyclicity gives invariance under both left and right translations. For left-invariant fields the Koszul identity reduces to $\nabla_XY=[X,Y]/2$: substituting this expression gives zero torsion and metric compatibility, since $\langle[X,Y],Z\rangle=-\langle Y,[X,Z]\rangle$. It follows by differentiating that geodesics are $\exp(tA)g$, and that parallel translation in a left-trivialized frame is $\exp(-t\operatorname{ad}_A/2)$. Its curvature is $R(X,Y)Z=-\operatorname{ad}_{[X,Y]}Z/4$, so $R(Y,X)X=-\operatorname{ad}_X^2Y/4$. The factor $1/4$ is retained throughout; rescaling the trace inner product does not change this connection. [F1, algebra]

1.2 The maps $r(g)=-g^{-1}$ and $r_i(g)=J_i gJ_i$ are commuting involutive isometries. Their fixed equations are $g^2=-I$ and $gJ_i=-J_i g$. Their common fixed set is smooth near each fixed point: in a normal-coordinate ball, an isometry fixing the center acts by its orthogonal derivative because it preserves geodesics and their initial velocities; hence the fixed set is the exponential of the common fixed linear subspace. The same description proves total geodesy. Its components are closed in the compact group. The ambient geodesic symmetry at a common fixed point commutes with each defining involution, so restricts to its component, proving that the component is symmetric. [F1, construct]

2.1 Differentiating $(\exp(tA)J_j)^2=-I$ at $t=0$ gives $AJ_j=-J_jA$; differentiating anticommutation with $J_i$ gives $AJ_i=J_iA$ for $i<j$. Conversely these relations imply the two defining equations for every $t$, and the continuous curve stays in the component through $J_j$. The fixed-space description in step 1.2 shows that these are exactly its tangent directions. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 In the real orthogonal two-plane decomposition of a skew generator, $\exp(A)=-I$ forces all rotation angles to be odd multiples of $\pi$. Consequently every geodesic from $I$ to $-I$ has length at least $\pi$ for the normalized metric. The group $\mathrm{SO}(p)$ is a nonempty connected compact boundaryless manifold; [F2] supplies a minimizing geodesic, so its distance between these endpoints is at least $\pi$. Every orthogonal complex structure $J$ gives $\cos(\pi t)I+\sin(\pi t)J$, of length $\pi$ and midpoint $J$. This proves the first midpoint assertion. Inductively let $K$ anticommute with $J_1,\ldots,J_j$ and set $J'=KJ_j^{-1}$. Then $(J')^2=-I$, $J'$ commutes with $J_i$ for $i<j$, and it anticommutes with $J_j$. Step 2.1 gives a path $\exp(\pi tJ')J_j$ in $P_j$ with midpoint $K$ and endpoints $\pm J_j$; it has length $\pi$. [A1, F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The component $P_j$ is nonempty, connected, compact and boundaryless by step 1.2; its metric is therefore complete. Since AC implies the countable-choice premise in [F2], Hopf–Rinow supplies a minimizing path in $P_j$ between $J_j$ and $-J_j$ whenever those endpoints lie in that component. Total geodesy makes it $\exp(tA)J_j$, with $\exp(A)=-I$ and the tangent relations of step 2.1. Set $J'=\exp(A/2)$. The odd rotation angles give $(J')^2=-I$; the tangent relations imply that $J'$ anticommutes with $J_j$ and commutes with its predecessors. Its midpoint $K=J'J_j$ therefore anticommutes with all $J_1,\ldots,J_j$. The path constructed from this $K$ in step 3.1 also lies in $P_j$ and has length $\pi$, so the minimum length is $\pi$ and the midpoint correspondence is exact. Taking components gives the assertion. The symmetry at $J_j$ is $g\mapsto J_jg^{-1}J_j$, whose formula is unchanged on replacing $J_j$ by $-J_j$; hence the indicated antipodes are poles. [A1, F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

[A1] The Axiom of Choice is assumed; it implies the countable-choice assumptions in the differential-geometric suppliers. No stronger choice principle is introduced. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The tangent conditions and totally geodesic trace-metric embedding hold; ambient parallel translation is $\exp(-t\operatorname{ad}_X/2)$ and its curvature operator is $-\operatorname{ad}_X^2/4$. ([[lem-clifford-centrioles-and-geodesic-tangent-condition]]).

[F2] The negative-square real Clifford classification determines the irreducible dimensions; there is one irreducible type except at indices congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. ([[thm-real-complex-clifford-algebra-classification]]).

[F3] The fixed-endpoint energy Hessian is twice the index form, and Killing variations are Jacobi fields. ([[thm-second-variation-formula-for-energy]], [[prop-killing-fields-restrict-to-jacobi-fields-along-geodesics]]).



**Proof technique:** direct construction.

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 Write $\gamma(t)=\exp(\pi tA)J_l$. By [F1], $A$ commutes with $J_i$ for $i<l$ and anticommutes with $J_l$. Split $\mathbb R^p$ orthogonally into minimal subspaces $M_h$ invariant under these operators. The symmetric operator $-A^2$ commutes with the family; hence on a minimal block it is $k_h^2I$. The endpoint equation $\exp(\pi A)=-I$ makes $k_h$ an odd positive integer. On that block $J'=A/k_h$ is a complex structure and $J_lJ'$ extends the Clifford family. The extended module is irreducible, since any proper invariant subspace would be invariant under $A$ and the original family. If all $k_h=1$, the geodesic has length $\pi$ and is minimal; otherwise some $k_h\ge3$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Now let $l=4m-2$ and put $i=J_1\cdots J_{l-1}$. Then $i^2=-I$; it commutes with $A$ and its predecessors and anticommutes with $J_l$. The complex eigenspaces of $A$ relative to $i$ are invariant under the whole family, because $J_l$ reverses both $A$ and $i$. Minimality gives $A=k_hi$ on each block, now with signed odd $k_h$, and the blocks are irreducible $C_l$ modules of size $s_l$. On two identified blocks $A=\operatorname{diag}(k_ji,k_hi)$. The same rotation computation gives $b=|k_j-k_h|/2$, and hence $b-1$ independent negative sine fields when $b\ge2$. Therefore

2.1 Suppose $l\not\equiv2\pmod4$. The unique irreducible $C_{l+1}$ type is equivalent to its last-generator sign reversal. Thus a pair $M_j,M_h$ may be isometrically identified preserving the first $l$ generators and reversing the extra generator. Orthogonalize an intertwiner $T$ by $T(T^*T)^{-1/2}$, which still intertwines. On the pair the generator becomes $\operatorname{diag}(k_jJ',-k_hJ')$. Put $B=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-I\\ I&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ there and zero elsewhere. It commutes with the original family, so conjugation by $\exp(uB)$ gives endpoint-fixed geodesics in $P_l$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 The Jacobi field of this variation is $[B,\gamma(t)]$. Put $b=(k_j+k_h)/2$. Substituting the two diagonal exponentials and transporting back by $\exp(-t\operatorname{ad}_{\pi A}/2)$ gives $2\sin(\pi bt)$ times a fixed nonzero off-diagonal matrix, up to a constant sign. Thus the field is $\sin(\pi bt)V_{jh}(t)$ for a nonzero parallel tangent field. Its curvature eigenvalue is $(\pi b)^2$, consistent with the ambient factor $1/4$. It is tangent intrinsically because it arises from the variation in step 2.1, and total geodesy preserves its tangent parallel translation. [F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For $a=1,\ldots,b-1$ set $W_{jh,a}(t)=\sin(\pi at)V_{jh}(t)$. These fields vanish at both endpoints and satisfy $I(W_{jh,a},W_{jh,a})=((\pi a)^2-(\pi b)^2)|V_{jh}|^2/2<0$. Sine orthogonality makes different modes orthogonal for $I$. Different unordered block pairs have disjoint off-diagonal support, preserved by parallel translation and curvature; hence their derivative and curvature pairings are zero in the trace metric. Their full span is therefore negative definite, not merely linearly independent. Fix one nonminimal block $h$. Each other block gives $b\ge2$ and at least one negative direction. There are $r-1$ such blocks, with $r=p/s_{l+1}$, proving the weak bound. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For the initial group stage $l=0$, split the skew generator into orthogonal real two-planes. On a pair of planes, the two commuting quaternionic $S^3$ factors of $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ have speeds $(k_j+k_h)/2$ and $(k_j-k_h)/2$ in units of $\pi$. A nonminimal plane paired with any other plane has a factor of absolute speed at least two. Its two perpendicular sine fields yield at least two negative directions. Their pair supports are orthogonal as in step 4.1, giving index at least $p-2$, and therefore at least $p/s_1-1$. The factorization can be checked directly by left and right multiplication by unit quaternions on $\mathbb H$; the tangent vectors with equal and opposite planar angles give its two orthogonal factors. [F1, F3, step 4.1, construct]
$$\operatorname{ind}\gamma\ge\sum_{k_j>k_h}\left(\frac{k_j-k_h}{2}-1\right).$$
All terms are nonnegative integers. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 The map $J\mapsto JJ_l^{-1}$ is complex linear relative to $i$. The determinant of the endpoint $-I$ equals one since $p$ is divisible by four, so its path determinant is a loop. The winding formula is $w=(s_l/4)\sum_h k_h$. Let $k_+$ be the sum of the positive $k_h$ and $k_-$ minus the sum of the negative ones. Then $k_++k_-\ge p/s_l$ and $k_+-k_-=4w/s_l$. The stated inequality implies $k_+,k_-\ge2d$. If some $k_j\ge3$, its pair contributions against the negative blocks sum to at least $(N_-+k_-)/2>d$, where $N_-\ge1$ is their number. If some $k_h\le-3$, reverse signs and use the positive blocks. Otherwise all entries are $\pm1$, making the path minimal. This proves the winding estimate with strictness exactly as stated. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

[A1] The Axiom of Choice is assumed; it implies the countable-choice assumptions in the differential-geometric suppliers. No stronger choice principle is introduced. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The preceding suspensions are $d$-connected in the stated size range, and the last path winding is $w=p/4-\eta$. ([[lem-iterated-suspension-and-winding-control-for-clifford-families]]).

[F2] For $l=k-1$, $p-4|w|\ge4ds_l$ makes all nonminimal indices greater than $d$, giving relative path shortening. ([[lem-real-clifford-block-rotation-index-lower-bound]], [[lem-relative-path-shortening-connectivity]]).

[F3] Finite CW inclusions have the relative homotopy extension property. ([[prop-relative-cw-inclusions-are-cofibrations]]).



**Proof technique:** direct construction.

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 The terminal winding is $w=p/4-\eta\ge0$, and $s_l=s_k$, so $p-4|w|=4\eta\ge4ds_l$. Apply [F2] to shorten the variable second path, fixing the prescribed parameter boundary. A minimal second path is determined by an invariant splitting $\mathbb R^p=L_0\oplus L_1$, with midpoint $+J_k$ on $L_0$ and $-J_k$ on $L_1$. Its determinant winding gives $\dim_{\mathbb C}L_1=\eta$. Combining with [F1] yields a $d$-connected map from the splitting space into the sphere mapping space. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 There is an additional correction on $L_0$: iterated suspension of its constant loop is a folded hemisphere map, not literally a constant sphere map. Its image lies in the closed hemisphere of the great sphere spanned by $I,J_1,\ldots,J_l$, with nonnegative $J_l$ coefficient, a product of nonnegative suspension sine factors. Write a point as $(y,a)$ with $a\ge0$ and $|y|^2+a^2=1$. Stereographic projection from $-J_l$ gives $z=y/(1+a)$ in the closed unit ball, with $I$ at $e_0$. Set $z_s=(1-s)z+se_0$ and

2.1 On $L_0$ the terminal loop is a path followed by its reverse. Contract it by replacing $\gamma(t)$ by $\gamma(st)$, $1\ge s\ge0$, before taking that concatenation. This is a based contraction continuous in the splitting projection. On $L_1$ the loop is the full positive Clifford circle. After the earlier suspensions the latter becomes the positive linear Hopf map, by expanding the cosine and sine suspension coordinates. [F1, step 1.1, construct]
$$y_s=\frac{2z_s}{1+|z_s|^2},\qquad a_s=\frac{1-|z_s|^2}{1+|z_s|^2}.$$
This contracts the hemisphere to $I$ while fixing $I$. Every sphere point remains an orthogonal Clifford matrix. Apply this on $L_0$ and keep the Hopf map on $L_1$. The universal scalar formulas and invariant projections make the homotopy continuous in the splitting. [step 2.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 The invariant splitting space is a compact Grassmannian. Its projection $P_1$ is recovered from the affine map by $P_1=(I-\phi(-e_0))/2$. Thus splitting-to-affine-map is a homeomorphism onto the affine subspace. Steps 2.1–3.1 show that the $d$-connected map of step 1.1 is homotopic to that homeomorphism followed by the actual affine inclusion. Homotopy invariance of relative homotopy groups therefore makes the inclusion $d$-connected. Equivalently, extend the resulting relative disk homotopies over cells, using [F3]. This last argument keeps arbitrary prescribed affine boundary maps fixed; it does not infer connectivity merely from a set-theoretic image. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, construct] ∎

**Given:** The bundle, Spin lift, AC and the indicated *ungraded* categories.

[F1] The negative-square Clifford classification gives
$C_{8m}=M_k(\mathbb R)$ and $C_{8m+4}=M_k(\mathbb H)$, with irreducible
column module $S=D^k$ ([[thm-real-complex-clifford-algebra-classification]]).

[F2] The associated spinor transition functions are left Clifford
multiplications, covering oriented orthonormal frame changes
([[def-given-spin-and-spinc-structures-and-associated-spinor-bundles]]).

[A1] AC is propagated through finite-bundle complements when these are used
([[cor-finite-cw-real-vector-bundle-has-orthogonal-complement-under-ac]]).



**Proof technique:** explicit symbols and finite-dimensional bundle constructions.

1.1 Write $A=M_k(D)$ and $S=D^k$ as a right $D$-space. Any real-linear endomorphism commuting with all matrix units has the same real-linear map $t:D\to D$ in every coordinate. Commuting also with left multiplication by every quaternion gives $t(a)=a\,t(1)$, so it is right multiplication $R_q$. In the real case this is just a real scalar. Composition satisfies $R_qR_r=R_{rq}$, so the commutant is $D^{\mathrm{op}}$. For $D=\mathbb H$ the map $q\mapsto R_{\bar q}$ is an additive, real-linear ring isomorphism $\mathbb H\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$. Conjugation, rather than inversion on arbitrary nonzero quaternions, is essential here. [F1, algebra]

2.1 For a left $A$-module $L$, the matrix idempotents split $L=\bigoplus_i e_{ii}L$. The maps $e_{i1}$ identify the summands with $e_{11}L$, a left $D$-space, so choosing a $D$-basis identifies $L$ with $S^{\oplus t}$. For $D=\mathbb H$, the proposed Hom action is additive in both variables, has unit, and satisfies $((f\cdot q)\cdot r)(s)=f(s\bar r\bar q)=f(s\overline{qr})$. The left action on $S$ satisfies $q\cdot(r\cdot s)=s\bar r\bar q=(qr)\cdot s$. Consequently evaluation is balanced, since $(f\cdot q)(s)=f(s\bar q)=f(q\cdot s)$. [step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 First take $L=S$. Its Hom is the commutant, and its right-$\mathbb H$ coordinate is $R_a\mapsto\bar a$, because $(R_a\cdot q)=R_{\bar q a}$ and $\overline{\bar q a}=\bar a q$. Under this coordinate evaluation is $\mathbb H\otimes_{\mathbb H}S\to S$, $h\otimes s\mapsto s\bar h$, the tensor-unit isomorphism for the left action just defined. For $L=S^{\oplus t}$ take its direct sum to obtain $\operatorname{Hom}_A(S,L)\otimes_{\mathbb H}S\cong L$. For $D=\mathbb R$ the identical argument uses ordinary scalar multiplication. For a right-$\mathbb H$ space $E$, the inverse identification is $E\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(S,E\otimes_{\mathbb H}S)$, $e\mapsto(s\mapsto e\otimes s)$; it is right-linear by the balancing identity and bijective after taking any finite basis of $E$. No dimension-only surjectivity assertion is needed. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 In a Spin frame, all these constructions have the fixed matrix form of steps 1.1–1.3. The right-$D$ action on the spinor commutes with every left Clifford multiplication, so it is preserved by the spinor transition functions in [F2]. Hom is a vector subbundle of the ordinary Hom bundle: locally it is the fixed kernel of finitely many matrix intertwining equations, of constant rank because the algebra and module types are locally constant. Changes of frame transport the Hom by conjugation and transport evaluation to evaluation. Thus the fiberwise isomorphisms are continuous bundle isomorphisms, glue globally, and commute with pullback and module morphisms. [F2, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 The inverse equivalences preserve direct sums and isomorphism classes, so they identify the additive monoids of bundles and hence their Grothendieck groups without any cancellation assumption. If a stable presentation is desired, a right-$\mathbb H$ bundle embeds in a finite trivial quaternionic bundle: finite charts and a partition give the quaternionic-linear embedding, and its invariant Hermitian orthogonal complement is quaternionic. The real proof is the same. Tensoring this complement with $\Sigma$ gives a module complement in a finite sum of $\Sigma$. This proves the stable-complement compatibility as well. Arbitrary graded modules were never substituted for the ungraded category. [A1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** AC, the given Spin bundle and the indicated rank.

[F1] The real Clifford–Thom supplier is
[[thm-real-clifford-thom-isomorphism]] with ungraded source
$K_{C(V)}(X)$ and positive rank $4m$; its map is precisely the
source-minus-target symbol $(\Lambda^+,\Lambda^-,c(v))$. Under EH's
north-section convention this map is the negative of
$[H(\Lambda)]-\pi^*[\Lambda^+]$, as restriction to the south disk shows.
This sign normalization is part of the interface. 

[F2] The Morita equivalences and the balanced scalar convention are proved
in the proposed [[lem-real-and-quaternionic-spinor-module-morita-evaluation]].

[F3] Relative symbols are functorial and their external product is the
total graded symbol ([[lem-reduced-relative-ko-suspension-exactness-and-product]]).

[F4] Given Spin lifts and associated spinor bundles use the repo convention $\operatorname{Spin}(0)=\{\pm1\}$ ([[def-given-spin-and-spinc-structures-and-associated-spinor-bundles]], [[def-real-clifford-group-and-normalized-pin-spin]]).



**Proof technique:** explicit symbols and finite-dimensional bundle constructions.

1.1 In either positive-rank branch compose the corresponding group isomorphism [F2] with [F1]. On a real bundle $E$, the volume operator on $E\otimes\Sigma$ is $1\otimes\omega$, so its eigenspaces are $E\otimes\Sigma^\pm$ and its clutching is $1\otimes c(v)$. Consequently the composite is exactly product by $\tau_V$, rather than an unspecified isomorphism. For a quaternionic bundle $E$ the same calculation is valid in the balanced tensor product since $\omega$ and $c(v)$ commute with the right scalar action on $\Sigma$. This gives exactly the stated $KSp$ formula. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 All constructions in step 1.1 commute with pullback of the Spin lift and of the vector bundle, proving naturality. In rank zero the repo convention is $\operatorname{Spin}(0)=\{\pm1\}$. A given lift is a double cover and its spinor is the associated sign line $L$. Its symbol is $[L]\in KO^0(X)$, so the map is $x\mapsto x[L]$, an isomorphism because the transition signs square to one and $L^{\otimes2}\cong\mathbb R$. For the canonical framed lift $L$ is trivial and this is the identity. This is separate from [F1] and preserves nontrivial rank-zero lifts. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For two real-branch ranks the graded tensor of the irreducible spinors is the irreducible real spinor for the orthogonal sum: its action is $c(v)\otimes1+\Gamma\otimes c(w)$; the square is $-(\lVert v\rVert^2+\lVert w\rVert^2)$ and the dimension is that of the unique simple ungraded matrix-algebra module. The product grading is the volume grading: in ranks divisible by four the product of the grouped Clifford generators gives $\omega_{V\oplus W}=\omega_V\otimes\omega_W$. The relative product rule [F3] therefore identifies the product symbols with the sum-bundle symbol. For quaternionic factors the same computation uses the balanced tensors and conjugation from [F2]. More explicitly, for two quaternionic ranks put $M=\Sigma_V\widehat\otimes\Sigma_W$ and $T=\operatorname{Hom}_{C(V\oplus W)}(\Sigma_{V\oplus W},M)$. Its real rank is four by the simple-module dimensions. The two balancing left-$\mathbb H$ actions on $M$ induce a commuting left-$\mathbb H\otimes\mathbb H$ action on $T$; these are even actions, so they commute with the volume grading. Evaluation in [F2] identifies $M=T\otimes_{\mathbb R}\Sigma_{V\oplus W}$. For right-quaternionic coefficient bundles $E,F$, the real coefficient of the sum is therefore exactly $(E\otimes_{\mathbb R}F)\otimes_{\mathbb H\otimes\mathbb H}T$. Associativity of balanced tensors identifies its spinor symbol with the product of the original symbols. Two quaternionic units accordingly produce real rank four, not rank one. If exactly one rank is quaternionic, the tensor spinor is quaternionic irreducible by the same dimension count, and the real coefficient tensors ordinarily with the quaternionic one. Thus all branches commute with their actual tensor symbols and proper coefficient operations. [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** AC and finite CW pairs, with nonpositive groups defined by suspension of the reduced bundle theory.

[F1] For a given Spin bundle of positive rank divisible by eight, tensoring real bundles with its volume-graded irreducible spinor followed by the volume-symbol Thom map is an isomorphism; its map is natural and compatible with tensor symbols ([[thm-spin-thom-isomorphism-rank-eight-multiples-and-rank-four-ksp]]).

[F2] Reduced and relative groups, suspension, natural exterior products of relative symbols, and their associativity and suspension interchange signs are established in [[lem-reduced-relative-ko-suspension-exactness-and-product]].



**Proof technique:** trivial rank-eight Thom map and split kernels.

1.1 Give the trivial oriented bundle $\mathbb R_X^8$ its framed Spin lift and let $\Sigma$ be its real irreducible Clifford module, graded by the volume involution. For a real bundle $E\to X$, its spinor module has volume eigenspaces $E\otimes\Sigma^\pm$ and symbol $1_E\otimes c(v)$. Thus the actual isomorphism [F1] is precisely $B_X:x\mapsto x\boxtimes\beta$ into $\widetilde{KO}^0(X_+\wedge S^8)$ by [F2]. This fixes the generator sign before any coefficient computation. Pullback commutes with the displayed eigenspaces and symbol, so $B_X$ is natural, and group completion gives the assertion for virtual bundles. [F1, F2, construct, algebra]

2.1 For based finite CW $Y$, basepoint evaluation splits $KO^0(Y)$ as $\widetilde{KO}^0(Y)\oplus KO^0(\mathrm{pt})$. Target restriction to the basepoint sphere $S^8$ is also split, by $Y\to\mathrm{pt}$. Naturality in step 1.1 gives a commuting square of these split projections with vertical maps $B_Y$ and $B_{\mathrm{pt}}$, both isomorphisms. The induced map on kernels is an isomorphism: injectivity is inherited, and a lift of an element of the target kernel has zero basepoint restriction because $B_{\mathrm{pt}}$ is injective. By the split quotient identification [F2], this is $\widetilde{KO}^0(Y)\cong\widetilde{KO}^0(Y\wedge S^8)$, with map again multiplication by $\beta$. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply step 2.1 to $Y=X/A$, using $X_+$ when $A$ is empty. It gives $KO^0(X,A)\cong KO^{-8}(X,A)$. Applying it to $S^k\wedge Y$ for $k\ge0$ gives $KO^{-k}(X,A)\cong KO^{-k-8}(X,A)$. Smash associativity and the suspension product convention of [F2] identify every one of these maps with multiplication by the same $\beta$. All spaces used remain finite CW; no arbitrary-base continuity assertion is needed. [F2, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 For any integer $j$, define its periodic continuation by the groups $KO^{j-8t}(X,A)$ for sufficiently large integers $t$ with $j-8t\le0$, identifying successive groups by the isomorphisms just proved. Formally this is the direct limit under multiplication by $\beta$ as $t$ increases. Since every transition is an isomorphism, each term maps isomorphically to the limit; all choices are canonically identified by finite composites of these maps. In nonpositive degrees this recovers the original groups. The same natural maps define every pair map and connecting map in positive degrees. Shifting $t$ proves the asserted periodicity for all $j$, rather than presupposing positive-degree groups or their periodicity. [step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Exterior products of the relative symbols are associative by [F2]. Therefore $(xy)\beta=x(y\beta)$ and $(x\beta)(y\beta)=(xy)\beta^2$ after the canonical rearrangement of sphere factors. The interchange sign involving the Bott sphere is $(-1)^{8k}=1$ in every suspended degree $k$. Consequently products pass to the continuation of step 4.1 independent of representatives, and $\beta$ becomes invertible there: its inverse is the unique coefficient sent to the unit by its isomorphism. This proves natural multiplicative periodicity on finite pairs and all degrees. The only choice assumption is that already used in the real Thom and relative bundle constructions [F1]–[F2]. [F1, F2, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** AC and the real bundle theory with its suspension grading.

[F1] Independent stable clutching calculations give $KO^0(\mathrm{pt})=\mathbb Z$, $KO^{-1}=KO^{-2}=\mathbb Z/2$, $KO^{-3}=0$, and $KSp^0(\mathrm{pt})=\mathbb Z$, $KSp^{-j}(\mathrm{pt})=0$ for $1\le j\le3$ ([[lem-real-and-symplectic-clutching-groups-in-low-degrees]]).

[F2] The trivial rank-four Spin bundle induces the natural isomorphism $KSp^0(Y)\to\widetilde{KO}^0(Y_+\wedge S^4)$ with the specified balanced quaternionic spinor symbol ([[thm-spin-thom-isomorphism-rank-eight-multiples-and-rank-four-ksp]]).

[F3] Multiplication by the same rank-eight symbol $\beta$ is an isomorphism on all finite pairs and integer degrees ([[thm-real-bott-periodicity-from-rank-eight-clifford-thom]]).



**Proof technique:** low clutching and the quaternionic rank-four boundary.

1.1 The first four groups are exactly [F1]. That proof uses components and the first two homotopy groups of stable $O$, independently of real Bott and of this table. Their integer and order-two generators are respectively the real line, the Möbius clutching and the one-turn stable orthogonal clutching. [F1]

1.2 For pointed finite CW $Y$, the isomorphism [F2] commutes with basepoint evaluation and with its split section. Its map on the basepoint summand is also an isomorphism. Hence it restricts to an isomorphism on the two kernels, namely $\widetilde{KSp}^0(Y)\cong\widetilde{KO}^0(Y\wedge S^4)$. Explicitly, any lift of a target-kernel element has zero basepoint restriction by injectivity on the basepoint group, which proves surjectivity on kernels; injectivity is inherited. [F2, algebra]

2.1 Taking $Y=S^j\wedge S^0$ for $j=0,1,2,3$ in step 1.2 gives $KO^{-4-j}(\mathrm{pt})\cong KSp^{-j}(\mathrm{pt})$. The second list in [F1] therefore supplies $\mathbb Z,0,0,0$ for degrees $-4,-5,-6,-7$. At $j=0$ the quaternionic line maps by the actual rank-four spinor symbol, fixing the stated generator. In the simultaneous case $TC$ is unitary and anticommutes with $H$; its square is $tc$, so the chiral involution is $TC$ for $tc=1$ and $iTC$ for $tc=-1$. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 Put $r=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $s=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $J=rs$. Then $r^2=s^2=1$, $J^2=-1$, and $J$ anticommutes with $r,s$. Send sign-reversed old generators to $x\otimes J$ and two new positive generators to $1\otimes r,1\otimes s$. Their squares and anticommutators prove a homomorphism $\mathrm{Cl}_{b+2,a}\to\mathrm{Cl}_{a,b}\otimes M_2(\mathbb R)$. Its image contains $1\otimes J$, hence all $x\otimes1$ and both tensor factors.
